item.title: Nuclear-geometry-tagging events in high-energy Ne--Ne collisions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nucleon-nucleon interactions within atomic nuclei give rise to collective properties such as deformation and nuclear clustering. Ultrarelativistic nucleon-nucleon collisions offer a novel way to probe the many-body correlations of the incoming nuclei, as the nuclear structure is reflected in the initial geometry of the produced system. State-of-the-art low-energy nuclear theory calculations predict highly deformed $^{20}$Ne nuclei with a characteristic $\alpha$+$^{16}$O bowling-pin-like shape. Since such nuclei have recently been collided at the LHC, investigating methods to maximise the sensitivity to the nuclear structure is pertinent. In this paper, we investigate whether body--body and tip--tip configurations of $^{20}$Ne nuclei can be identified in Monte--Carlo Glauber simulations using geometry-sensitive observables: the eccentricity, $\varepsilon_2$, and the transverse compactness, $d_\perp$. The nuclear configurations are obtained from nuclear lattice effective field theory calculations within the framework of Nuclear Lattice Effective Field Theory (NLEFT) and $\textit{ab initio}$ Projected Generator Coordinate Method (PGCM). We utilise a Fisher linear discriminant to select body--body and tip--tip configurations based on the $\varepsilon_2$-$d_\perp$ correlation. With classifier thresholds chosen to retain $30\%$ of the target class in a validation sample, the two-variable Fisher selection obtains purities in NLEFT (PGCM) of $0.201$ ($0.156$) and $0.573$ ($0.540$) for body--body and tip--tip events, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Joachim Carlo Kristian Bjerg Hansen, Emil Gorm Dahlb{\ae}k Nielsen

item.title: Relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in the Density Frame for heavy-ion collisions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a numerical study of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in the Density Frame for boost-invariant flows in 2+1 dimensions. The Density Frame is a formulation of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics that is first order in time, requires no auxiliary fields, and has no non-hydrodynamic modes; the only parameters are the shear and bulk viscosities and the equation of state. We formulate the numerical method in terms of a discrete analog of the dissipative function, which guarantees that the discrete equations produce entropy on all length scales and leads to a remarkably robust algorithm. We test the method against the exact solution of kinetic theory in the relaxation time approximation with Gubser symmetry. In making this comparison, we clarify how the kinetic solution matches onto hydrodynamics: we organize the solution by the opacity and show how the Bjorken attractor passes onto the Gubser solution order by order in gradients. We then replace the hydrodynamic engine of the MUSIC code with the Density Frame, and compare the two for IP-Glasma initial conditions in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02$ TeV. The Density Frame smooths sharp gradients more rapidly. The largest differences arise in the bulk-viscous sector, where the bulk pressure in the Density Frame responds instantaneously to the flow, while in the M\"uller-Israel-Stewart-based MUSIC it relaxes over a finite time. With shear viscosity alone, the multiplicity, mean transverse momentum, and elliptic flow of final-state hadrons from the two codes are very similar. The Density Frame is now ready for a complete Bayesian analysis of heavy-ion data.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Paquet, Mayank Singh, Derek Teaney

item.title: Incorporating deep neural networks into lepton-nucleus interaction modeling
item.description: arXiv:2610.40912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a scheme to incorporate precise inclusive cross-section predictions from a deep neural network trained on electron--carbon scattering data into a Monte Carlo event generator. The inclusive prediction is decomposed into independent exclusive interaction channels using the generator's theoretical models, and the resulting events are reweighted accordingly. We apply this scheme to investigate nuclear effects in inclusive and semi-exclusive electron-scattering measurements.
item.dc:creator: Hemant Prasad, Jan T. Sobczyk, Krzysztof M. Graczyk, Beata E. Kowal, Rwik Dharmapal Banerjee, J. Luis Bonilla

item.title: Is XTE J1814-338 a dark matter-admixed neutron star?
item.description: arXiv:2610.41293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore the possibility that the ultracompact object XTE J1814-338 is a dark matter-admixed neutron star (DNS) based on a general-relativistic two-fluid approach, in which one fluid describes ordinary nuclear matter and the other dark matter. The equations of state of nuclear matter and dark matter are described by the Brueckner-Hartree-Fock (BHF) theory with realistic three-body forces and a generic bosonic self-interacting dark matter model, respectively. Based on the observational data, we determine the parameter space for XTE J1814-338 as a DNS, and find that only a halo stellar configuration with a high dark matter fraction is allowed. Furthermore, we predict other observable properties of XTE J1814-338 and provide robust lower bounds for these quantities.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Ming Liu, Peng-Cheng Chu, He Liu, Zeng-Hua Li, Xiao-Hua Li

item.title: The role of spin polarization in event-by-event fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2610.41386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The event-by-event initial state fluctuations constitute a critical physical quantity for understanding the dynamics of high-energy heavy-ion collisions. Due to the extremely limited available experimental data of such fluctuations, it is difficult to constrain or direct the characterization of the underlying initial state properties. This work constrains the correlation function between the initial eccentricity and the asymmetry by employing a parton distribution function that incorporates spin polarization induced by thermal vorticity and thermal shear. Based on the kinetic theory calculations, we found that the asymmetry fluctuations considering spin polarization have a significant splitting effect compared to those without spin polarization. These splitting exhibit pronounced system size and energy dependence. Moreover, the ratios of correlation function display similar system size and energy dependence--particularly in the low-temperature regime ($T \lesssim$ 0.12 GeV). These results suggest that spin polarization may serve as a useful constraint method for the event-by-event initial state fluctuations of heavy-ion collisions.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Ying He, Li-Juan Zhou, Li-Xin Yang, Qian-Qian Du, De-Xian Wei

item.title: Color transparency effects on the deuteron spin observables in the hard $pd \to ppn$ reaction
item.description: arXiv:2610.41767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The pionless breakup of a deuteron induced by 15 GeV/$c$ beam proton is considered theoretically in the kinematics where both outgoing protons are fast and the neutron is slow in the rest frame of the deuteron. Significant influence of color transparency on the deuteron vector and tensor analyzing powers is expected.
item.dc:creator: A. B. Larionov

item.title: Algebraic models of alpha-cluster nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.42015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this contribution I review the algebraic cluster model (ACM) for $\alpha$-conjugate nuclei with $A=4n$ and its extension to the cluster shell model (CSM) for $A=4n+x$ nuclei. The CSM describes the splitting of single-particles levels in a deformed field generated by the cluster of $\alpha$-particles. As an example, I discuss the energies, electromagnetic transitions and form factors of the neighboring nuclei $^{12}$C and $^{13}$C.
item.dc:creator: Roelof Bijker

item.title: A systematic study of hydrodynamic attractors in periodically driven systems at weak and strong couplings
item.description: arXiv:2610.40877v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study equilibration and hydrodynamic response in conformal systems undergoing periodic expansion and contraction along one spatial direction. Using strongly coupled holography (AdS/CFT), weakly coupled kinetic theories (relaxation-time approximation, scalar $\phi^4$ theory and the Yang--Mills sector of QCD effective kinetic theory) and hydrodynamics (Navier--Stokes, M\"uller--Israel--Stewart (MIS) and rBRSSS), we investigate the shear response to a periodic drive of varying amplitude $A$ and frequency $\omega$, both analytically in linear response and numerically. We find that, at the linear level, $A\ll 1$, periodically driven systems approach a cyclic attractor that in general differs from Navier--Stokes behaviour. This attractor is universal among kinetic theories and accurately described by MIS theory: for slow driving, $\omega \tau_\pi \ll 1$, where $\tau_\pi$ is the shear relaxation time, it approaches the Navier--Stokes limit, whereas for fast driving the shear stress saturates at its non-interacting (free-streaming) value. In strongly coupled holographic systems, the periodic drive excites non-hydrodynamic quasinormal modes, which produce a characteristic ringing in the approach to the cyclic attractor, in contrast to the purely exponential approach found in kinetic theories. This difference is a direct consequence of the distinct non-hydrodynamic spectra of the two classes of theories. Moreover, unlike in kinetic theory, the holographic response is sensitive to the curvature terms of second-order hydrodynamics. Over longer times, non-linear viscous heating, which is quadratic in the drive amplitude, raises the temperature and thereby lowers $\omega\tau_\pi$, since $\tau_\pi\sim 1/T$. This induces a slow drift of the cyclic attractor, which eventually converges towards Navier--Stokes hydrodynamics at asymptotically late times.
item.dc:creator: Aleksas Mazeliauskas, Toshali Mitra, S\"oren Schlichting, Simon Schneider, Louis Nwakile Onwuka, Martin Vrdoljak

item.title: The Importance of Curium-250 to the $\gamma$-Ray Signature of $r$-Process Remnants
item.description: arXiv:2610.40907v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Identifying the astrophysical sites of the heavy rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) remains one of the most prominent unsolved problems in nuclear astrophysics. Emitted $\gamma$-rays from the decay of unstable nuclei have been identified as a potential observable marker on both prompt and delayed timescales which could provide conclusive evidence of the presence of $r$-process activity. In this work, we identify and discuss the importance of $^{250}$Cm to the $\gamma$-ray spectra of remnants, showing that the decay spectrum of $^{250}$Cm dominates the $\gamma$-ray spectra of $r$-process ejecta across a broad timescale ($\sim$ 2,000 - 20,000 years). We highlight the uncertain nature of this spectra: $^{250}$Cm may decay via $\alpha$-decay, $\beta$-decay, and spontaneous fission, but the decay branchings are not experimentally known, and each decay channel produces unique spectral lines which may be observable. We examine the potential for observation of the most prominent spectral signatures, finding that for conventional neutron star merger remnants, $\gamma$-ray lines will be detectable in current and future detectors only in the very near galaxy ($\sim$ 1 kpc), but other sites which could produce a larger ejecta mass may have greater observable distances. Our findings highlight the potential of actinide decay chains to indicate r-process nucleosynthesis and further underscore the necessity of measuring the nuclear properties that define their characteristic spectral signatures.
item.dc:creator: Axel Gross, Samuel Cupp, G. Wendell Misch, Matthew R. Mumpower

item.title: Two gluon fusion into a $\pi^0$, $\eta$, or $\eta'$ in a relatively weak magnetic field
item.description: arXiv:2610.41020v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we investigate gluon fusion as a mechanism for neutral meson production ($\pi^0$, $\eta$, and $\eta'$), in the phenomenological context of heavy-ion collisions prior to thermalization, in which a large gluon multiplicity is expected, and when an intense background magnetic field is expected to arise. For this purpose, we computed the ratios of the emission probability rates in the presence of the background magnetic field as compared to vacuum (zero-field), as a function of transverse momenta $p_T$ and energy $\sqrt{s}$, close to midrapidity. Our theoretical results suggest a catalytic effect from the presence of the background magnetic field, that may enhance the neutral pion production by several orders of magnitude at very small energies $s \lesssim 1~\text{GeV}^2$, while the effect is negligible at larger energies $s\gtrsim 10~\text{GeV}^2$. In contrast, the $\eta$ and $\eta'$ production rates are nearly insensitive to the magnetic field presence (as compared to vacuum).
item.dc:creator: Fabio L. Braghin, Enrique Mu\~noz

item.title: Deconfinement in weak electric and magnetic fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.41066v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the thermal deconfinement transition in weak electric and magnetic fields, describing the hadronic phase by a pion gas and the quark--gluon plasma by the MIT bag model. Besides the thermal response of each phase, we include the one-loop electromagnetic vacuum terms of quarks and charged pions, renormalized at a common scale that fixes the charge in the confined vacuum. With no fitting of the electromagnetic response, the critical temperature rises with the electric field and falls with the magnetic one. The electric curvature is of the same size as that obtained on the lattice, while the magnetic one is a few times larger. We discuss the dependence on quark mass and renormalization scale, and a large-$N_c$ organization of both curvatures, whose sum is independent of the vacuum terms and connects directly to perturbative QCD.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo S. Fraga, Leticia F. Palhares

item.title: Two-Fluid Radial Stability of Dark-Matter-Admixed Compact Objects: Dark Compact Planets, Dark White Dwarfs, Dark Neutron Stars, and Dark Oysters
item.description: arXiv:2610.41082v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the equilibrium structure and stability against radial oscillations of a variety of two-fluid compact objects containing ordinary baryonic matter admixed with cold dark matter coupled through the background spacetime. For the ordinary fluid, we employ a QCD equation of state compatible with chiral effective field theory at nuclear densities (supplemented by the BPS and Negele-Vautherin models at extremely low densities) and with perturbative QCD in the high-density regime while also satisfying also current astrophysical data. For the dark fluid, we assume self-interacting fermionic matter with particle masses of $m_f=$ 2, 5, 10, and 100 GeV and two self-interaction strengths of $y=0.1$ and $10^3$. By scanning a large range of central pressures for both fluids, we identify the presence of dark compact planets, dark white dwarfs, dark neutron stars and the so-called dark oysters. Importantly, these objects are not only in two-fluid hydrostatic equilibrium, but they are also stable against two-fluid radial oscillations. We find that the relative representation of each class in the radially stable sample is strongly sensitive to the combinations of $m_f$ and $y$, with some combinations entirely suppressing some of these object classes within the sampled domain while favoring others. In addition to these classes, strong self-repulsion supports stable, dark-matter-dominated branches with compact ordinary-matter cores and extended dark halos, approaching the self-interacting fermion-star limit. Finally, we calculate the gravitational redshift at the ordinary-matter surface, $z_{\rm OM}$, including the contribution of extended dark-matter halos for which we found radially stable configurations with $z_{\rm OM}>2$.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e C. Jim\'enez, Oscar Pastor, Laura Tolos

item.title: Characterizing $\pT$-differential Radial-Flow Fluctuations in Au+Au Collisions at FAIR with a Multi-Phase Transport Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.41607v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We report the first predictions of the transverse-momentum ($\pT$)-differential radial-flow fluctuation observable, $\vzpT$, in Au+Au collisions at the top SIS100 energy, $\snn=4.9$~GeV, which will be available at the FAIR accelerator complex. Radial flow and its fluctuations are studied for different centrality intervals and reference-$\pT$ selections to investigate the properties and robustness of the calculated long-range correlation. $\vzpT$ displays a characteristic evolution from negative values at low $\pT$ to positive values at higher $\pT$. The integrated $v_0$, obtained with different reference-$\pT$ intervals, follows a common trend, with an approximately inverse-square-root dependence on the inclusive charged-particle multiplicity ($\nch$). The $\vzpT$ signal changes little when the pseudorapidity gap is varied between 0.2 and 0.8, or when the edges of the reference-$\pT$ interval are varied, in the bulk region. For identified particles, the pion and proton $\vzpT$ are ordered at low $\pT$, qualitatively similar to the mass ordering seen at higher energies. However, unlike at higher collision energies, $\vzpT$ does not exhibit constituent-quark scaling, so the results do not support an interpretation in terms of partonic collectivity. These results provide constraints on the evolution of radial correlations toward lower collision energies and motivate comparisons with complementary observables to clarify their connection to collective dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Sanchari Thakur, Partha Pratim Bhaduri

item.title: Meson spectroscopy from lattice QCD
item.description: arXiv:2610.42037v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Determining the meson spectrum directly from Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) remains a central challenge, since QCD is strongly coupled at low energies and most excited states appear as resonances in hadronic decay channels. Advances in lattice QCD and scattering theory now provide a systematic framework for extracting meson spectra and resonance properties from first principles. Here I present an overview of this program and review current state-of-the-art calculations in meson spectroscopy from lattice QCD. I highlight recent progress in the extraction of resonant and coupled-channel amplitudes, along with frontier developments in three-body dynamics and the determination of meson photo-couplings. Together, these advances are bringing us closer to a comprehensive first-principles description of the excited meson spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Andrew W. Jackura

item.title: Bayesian inference of the dense matter equation of state built upon extended Skyrme interactions: A generalization
item.description: arXiv:2607.09369v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The nonrelativistic theory of nuclear matter (NM) based on Brussels-Skyrme interactions is employed to develop models for dense and neutron-rich matter within a Bayesian framework. We employ the following set of constraints: the four best-known nuclear empirical parameters, the density dependence of the energy per particle in pure neutron matter (PNM), the density dependence of the Landau effective mass ($m_\mathrm{eff}$) of neutrons in PNM and symmetric NM, and a lower limit on the maximum gravitational mass that neutron stars (NSs) can support. In addition, a number of ``sanity checks'' are added: the values of the speed of sound, neutron and proton Landau effective masses, and Fermi velocities are constrained up to the central density of the most massive NS configuration and for isospin asymmetries $\delta=(n_n-n_p)/(n_n+n_p)$ ranging from 0 to 1. Our ensemble of models \emph{fully} explores the capacity of nonrelativistic Brussels-Skyrme effective interactions to describe NM at densities exceeding several times the nuclear saturation density. This is a necessary step toward a better understanding of the properties of dense matter and possible correlations between the parameters of NSs and the parameters of NM. Due to the pronounced U-shaped density dependencies of $m_\mathrm{eff}$, which qualitatively agree with the predictions of ab initio calculations featuring three-body forces, all our models exhibit a non-monotonic ``rise-and-fall'' behavior of the thermal pressure ($p_\mathrm{th}$) as a function of density, which in extreme cases leads to $p_\mathrm{th} < 0$. This work is a generalization of [Beznogov and Raduta, Phys. Rev. C 110, 035805 (2024)].
item.dc:creator: Mikhail V. Beznogov, Adriana R. Raduta

item.title: $\Lambda$(1520) as a probe of resonance-driven deuteron formation at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2606.10668v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Light nuclei such as deuterons are produced abundantly in high-energy proton-proton and nuclear collisions despite their tiny binding energies. Their production mechanism remains unresolved, as both nucleon coalescence and statistical thermal models reproduce inclusive LHC yields. We propose a direct invariant-mass observable that discriminates between these scenarios using the long-lived $\Lambda(1520) \to {\rm pK}$ resonance. If decay protons coalesce into deuterons, the produced nuclei remain correlated with the kaon, allowing the resonance peak to be reconstructed experimentally through proxy masses, $M_{\rm (d/2)K}$, formed from kaons and half the deuteron four-momentum. Using Thermal-FIST and PYTHIA with a deuteron coalescence afterburner, we show that a $M_{\rm (d/2)K}$ peak emerges only in the coalescence scenario. This observable provides a direct experimental probe of resonance-fed deuteron production and of late-stage coalescence dynamics in high-energy collisions.
item.dc:creator: Sushanta Tripathy, Peter Christiansen

item.title: Properties of the $D_{s0}^*(2317)^\pm$ in hot and dense nuclear matter
item.description: arXiv:2608.01272v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the properties of the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^\pm$ in hot and dense nuclear matter using a coupled-channel molecular model built on next-to-leading-order heavy meson chiral perturbation theory. In-medium modifications to the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ stem from changes to the $DK$ channel within the coupled $DK$-$D_s \eta$ system. As nuclear density increases, the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ quasiparticle peak shifts toward lower energies and broadens, tracking the behavior of the $D$-meson spectral function. As for temperature effects, those are milder, with the thermal smearing of the Fermi surface and the melting of $\Sigma_c N^{-1}$ excitations in the $D$-meson spectral function shifting the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ peak back toward its free-space mass while narrowing it. Conversely, the behavior of the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$ is governed by the $\bar D \bar K$ channel and its medium behavior is driven by the $\bar K$ spectral function. With increasing temperature, the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$ also approaches its free-space mass, but its width broadens before saturating at high temperatures. Incorporating explicit medium dependencies into the interaction kernel, driven by density and/or temperature variations in the pion decay constant, further shifts the $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^+$ mass lower and narrows its width with temperature. As for $D_{s0}^\ast(2317)^-$, its mass also drops with temperature but its width increases. These contrasting medium behaviors offer a promising pathway to constrain the internal structure of these exotic states.
item.dc:creator: Tomona Kinugawa, \`Angels Ramos, Laura Tolos

item.title: Complex potential and the thermal width of quarkonium in quark-gluon plasma
item.description: arXiv:2610.40220v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the complex heavy quark anti-quark potential in lattice 2+1 flavor QCD at non-zero temperature. We point out a close relation between the imaginary part of the potential and the thermal quarkonium width. Using this relation, we estimate the thermal width of charmonia and bottomonia at high temperatures, which are not yet accessible with direct lattice QCD calculations of the quarkonium correlation functions and compare these to the results of the T-matrix analysis. For some of the excited quarkonia states, our estimates of the thermal width are smaller than the ones obtained in the T-matrix analysis.
item.dc:creator: Rasmus Normann Larsen, Peter Petreczky, Jorge Luis Dasilva Golan, Johannes H. Weber
